utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have now concluded the taking of evidence from a witness in closed session. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, with the exception of I think a very small number of outstanding matters, the Prosecution has no further witnesses to call. I have just been reminded, in fact, instructed by my case manager, who has received instructions from Ms. Guduric, however, that I must inform the Trial Chamber that a translation of exhibit P00049.094 has now been uploaded into e-court. And the same goes, Your Honour, for a translation of exhibit P00072. That has now been uploaded into e-court. I was going to say, Your Honour, that the Prosecution has no further witnesses to call, and with the exception of a few matters that I believe are currently pending before the Trial Chamber, that is the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Most, if not all, of those outstanding evidentiary issues should be dealt with in the course of tomorrow, if not today. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you would allow me, I would want to go back to the question that you said I could put after the examination of the witness. I would like to tender into evidence -- I would like for the document 1D285 marked for identification, which is in tab 42, which is the employment contract of Mr. Zoran Krstevski, I would like to tender this document into evidence, since this is not, as the Prosecutor said, a large document of the interior ministry. This is a true document of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and after the re-examination, it is clear that this document can be tendered into evidence. Maybe its probative value can be assessed. The Prosecutor showed the document of Branko Bojcevski, the state secretary of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and then of Blagoja Jakovoski - Jakovoski, I'm sorry - where there was a quotation where allegedly Blagoja Jakovoski as the body-guard of the minister had seen --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the end of the statement before --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This very fact clearly shows that it is possible for all of these persons, Venko Kalacoski and Zoran Krstevski, were actually employed in the Ministry of Interior Affairs but it is questionable from -- since when, because Venko Kalacoski could not have been state secretary in times when Branko Bojcevski was state secretary, and Branko Bojcevski from the statements shown by the Prosecutor was clearly state secretary until November 2001 when he was replaced by Venko Kalacoski. Therefore, if we take into consideration everything that Gigi or Blagoja Jakovoski testified before this Court concerning the timing, does not at all decrease the probative value of this evidence, which is an official document of the Ministry of Interior which shows that Zoran Krstevski started to work in the Ministry of Interior Affairs on 27th of September, 2001. Therefore, after the re-examination as well, the Defence still considers there are enough elements for this document to be admitted into evidence. And there is no reason why it should only remain marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the Prosecution's submission, the indications that were described during re-examination certainly cast a cloud, a large and dark cloud, over the veracity of the information in this contract that has been offered for admission. And therefore, in the Prosecution's submission, the Defence has not demonstrated that it has sufficient probative value for it to be admitted at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document marked for identification will be received as an exhibit. Clearly, the question of its veracity or whether there was some other arrangement before it came into existence are matters which will need to be considered by the Chamber in due course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will retain the same number but will become Exhibit 1D285.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any outstanding issue, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. These are not very major issues. For the Exhibit 2D42 we have an official translation and it is updated under -- uploaded in the e-court under 2T42. It's the same with the Exhibit 2D47. It has been uploaded in the e-court under 65 ter 2D423. So instead of 2D, it should stand 423, in line 16. So line 16, it should say 65 ter 2D422.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want the official translation now included in that exhibit; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That can be managed. If we can find the right number.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat once again, Your Honours. Maybe it would be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What about 2D422. Does that make you happy? [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the -- for the Exhibit 2D42, we have received an official translation from the CLSS, and was uploaded in e-court under number 65 ter 2D422. It is the same with Exhibit 2D47. We received an official translation, and was uploaded in e-court under 65 ter 2D423. And we would like to add them to the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Those matters will be attended to, Mr. Apostolski. Is there any other further --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- outstanding matter? Can we revert, then, to the question of the timetabling of the steps that must be taken between this point and the opening of the Defence case. Is there any further matter that needs to be raised, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I certainly do not want to be presumptuous and jump the gun. I'm certainly aware of the matters of Rule 65 ter (G), but I assume that is what the Chamber is going to discuss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I may have some additional matters to raise after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see no indication from counsel of anything further than was said the other day. When we heard these submissions the other day, counsel for both Defences stressed that the orthodox celebrations of Christmas and new year in Macedonia were on the 7th and 14th of January, and -- respectively and attention was also drawn to the difficulty of effectively contacting and dealing with potential Defence witnesses over the period between the two different religious celebrations of at least the Christmas festival. It was proposed that some three to four weeks outside the holiday period should be allowed for the disclosures required by Rule 65 ter (G), between that disclosure and the commencement of the Defence evidence. Sorry, allowed until the disclosures were made as required by Rule 65 ter (G). The Prosecution was concerned that, in addition to the time sought by the Defence, it should have adequate time for investigation and preparation following the disclosures by the Defence, and that that time should be allowed before Defence evidence commenced to be led. Now, of course, if those things are put together, they seem to take us to the second half of February, and -- no, the second half of February, if those things are all put together, and it is the view of the Chamber that the time allowed between the close of the Prosecution case and the commencement of the Defence case should be as short a period as fairness will allow. Therefore, the Chamber has come to a view that something less attractive perhaps, less relaxed in time than seem to be the hope of counsel, should be ordered, but it does recognise that things must be done that will take time and that there be some inhibition from the holiday period in the capacity to attend to some of those matters and it also recognises that the Prosecution must have some time. In the view of the Chamber, it would order, making these orders pursuant to Rule 65 ter (M) in lieu of the Pre-Trial Judge: Firstly that the Rule 65 ter (G) disclosure, all of this as required by that Rule for both Defences should be completed. That is, filed and served in full compliance with the Rule by noon on Thursday, the 10th of January. That, of course, is over a month from now. It proposes that there should be a pre-Defence conference on Monday, the 28th of January and the commencement of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski should be on Tuesday, the 29th of January. Is there any serious difficulties seen with any of those dates? If not, they will be the dates ordered. We feel that any greater time allowance would be going beyond what fairness really required. We are anxious, as I'm sure everyone is, that we get on with the completion of this case as quickly and efficiently as possible. We would, there being nothing else, therefor plan to adjourn now with a view to the Chamber reassembling for the continuation of the evidence at the end of January on the dates indicated. We would wish all well for the coming respective festive seasons, and we look forward to seeing you refreshed and invigorated for the new year. Mr. Saxon, are you refreshed or invigorated?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm both, Your Honour. I have just received some more strict instructions, that I make a general request that all transcripts of video-clips that have been shown as part of Prosecution exhibits be admitted. I'm not -- sorry, this was simply a request that was passed to me a few moments ago, and I don't know if I'm expressing it as clearly as I should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I hear you enough to say to you we need a written motion, because that will be a very significant number of individual pieces of evidence, particularly some of the video-clips and they will need to be identified precisely not only as to exhibit number but as to the particular time sections of each that were -- you want to have admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you may have leave to move that motion in writing, and we would ask if there is any objection to any part of it, that that objection by either Defence be made in writing within ten days of being served with the written motion, and we would hope to be able to produce an order in respect of the motion without needing to hear anybody in respect of it. Well, if that's the case, I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, very sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Two matters, two perhaps related matters. It would be helpful in terms of the preparation of the Prosecution for the Defence case to know sooner, rather than later, if one or both of the accused intend to testify, because obviously, this requires a great deal of preparation. And related to that is a perhaps a procedural question, and that is whether if one or both of the accused decides to testify, at what point in their respective defence case they would give evidence, because there's certainly an argument to be made that such evidence would have more weight, more value, if it is given at the start of a Defence case rather at the end. And so I simply wanted to raise that first matter and wondering whether the Defence can give any indication about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the order we have made would suggest that that need not be answered before the 10th of January. If either Defence counsel is in a position privately to assist Mr. Saxon before then, we would encourage that, but we will not make -- could not make any other order in respect of the matter. We would add, in respect of your second point of concern, that the practice which the Chamber considers extremely desirable, is for the -- an accused to give evidence first, rather than at some other time in the course of his Defence case, because, in that way, the Chamber is able to not be distracted by concerns about passages of evidence being -- by an accused being shaped to conform to evidence given by other Defence witnesses. A problem that can distract from the force and reliance that can be placed on the evidence of an accused. But we leave the matter with those words of advice and encouragement to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I maybe one more point, Your Honour. It is simply this, that the -- in the past, the Prosecution has interviewed one of the accused, Mr. Boskoski. There is a transcript of that interview, and the Prosecution may seek to use portions of that interview during the cross-examination of Defence witnesses. It's a matter I have raised very briefly some days ago with Defence counsel. And the Prosecution realises that particularly because we have a co-accused in this case that there are certain legal issues that might arise during the course of such cross-examination. Therefore, the Prosecution may, before the start of the Defence case file a motion seeking the permission of the Chamber to use the transcript of the prior interview of the accused Boskoski during cross-examination of Defence witnesses. I simply wanted to alert everyone to that; that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is a matter we must leave for you, Mr. Saxon. One of the decisions to be delivered shortly by the Chamber will deal with at least issues relevant to that consideration. And there has been a recent decision of the Appeals Chamber that might also be considered by counsel, which has been -- will be mentioned in the decision of this Chamber. Before somebody thinks of something else, we will adjourn. But I do so, wanting to convey our appreciation to all those in and around the courtroom who have assisted and supported us during the year. We're very grateful and we look forward to your reinvigoration and rest as well and we wish you well during the coming season. We now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 28th day of January, 2008

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.30 p.m.,
